title: "1 Identify available methods"
link-citations: true
---

## Definition
These studies aim to identify methods that can address a specific research challenge. They often combine identification with a structured characterization or comparison of methods, e.g., by describing definitions, key features, variants, assumptions, strengths, or limitations.

## Typical approaches and corresponding examples
[Scoping reviews of methods research](../approaches/11scoping-review.qmd): identify causal methods to allow predictions under hypothetical interventions;[@Lin2021a] identify definitions of intention-to-treat;[@Alshurafa2012inconsistent] identify criteria for assessing the credibility of subgroup analyses;[@Schandelmaier2019a] identify factors influencing the trustworthiness of non-randomized studies;[@Adegboye2025factors] identify methods addressing bias in adaptive trial designs;[@Robertson2023point] characterizing methods for group-variable selection.[@Buch2023a]

[Reviews of applied or planned methods](../approaches/9review-applied.qmd): to identify types of initial data analysis in observational studies.[@Huebner2020hidden]
